body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal R(P_X)=A_q(P_X)\), where \(A_q\) is the finite exact-real reconstruction algorithm of Theorem~\textnormal{thm:finite-exact-aq-reconstruction}.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from the exact observed law \(P_X\); the optional empirical rung observes \(n\) independent response vectors.
sampling_model.units: Independent respondents with common categorical response law \(P_X\) only in the empirical rung.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the latent measurement graph, latent law, and latent DAG Markov-equivalence class.
sampling_model.overlap: Every latent configuration has positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated in the population results; empirical queried marginals use cell proportions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For binary latent variables, double triangularity yields full-rank views, identifies the latent dimension, and identifies the model under third-view and subset conditions.

Under completeness, nondegeneracy, two sufficient measurements, and the stated support condition, a mixed-type discrete latent structure and its latent MEC are identified by tensor-rank and discretization arguments.
Three finite latent-class views are generically identifiable up to label swapping when their Kruskal ranks meet the stated inequality.
Population tensor unfoldings constructively identify a \(Q\)-matrix when every latent attribute has at least two pure items.
A measurement graph and latent law can be reconstructed from a mixture oracle under no-twins, maximality, nondegeneracy, and subset conditions.
Binary restricted latent-class \(Q\)-matrices admit checkable strict and generic identifiability criteria.
Observable response restrictions yield calibrated goodness-of-fit tests for a provisional cognitive-diagnosis \(Q\)-matrix.

body.tldr: The field-tier contribution for \(q\ge3\) is an explicit product \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\) of context-specific \(q\times q\) determinants for a novel categorical double-triangular condition. The determinant identity gives the exact full-rank frontier, is nonzero on an explicitly constructed relatively open dense full-measure subset of every fixed positive categorical-table parameter space, yields \(K_{\min}(P_X)=K\), and supports same-\(K\) quotient identification over a fully enumerated BLCM comparison domain. The identification argument isolates a new observable coordinate-alignment step: generic three-view uniqueness returns \(q^K\) anonymous mixture labels, while component-equality patterns recover \(K\) \(q\)-state coordinates and the latent MEC. A dimensionally consistent positive \(q=3,K=3,J=8\) model displays all six certificate matrices and has no pure child for its third latent coordinate. A separately typed \(q_{\mathrm{bin}}=2\) comparator records exactly the assumptions and conclusions of Lee and Gu's binary Theorems 1--2. Chen et al.'s mixed-type completeness and two-sufficient-measurement class is formally incomparable and does not cover the equal-\(q\) witness. The open rung is a terminating sound-and-complete reconstruction algorithm and a calibrated \(\texttt{cdmTools}\)-style diagnostic.

project_justification.gap: Binary double triangularity uses scalar contrasts, whereas for \(q\ge3\) ordinary nondegeneracy permits a local conditional determinant to vanish. Generic Kruskal theory neither locates the failing graph context nor aligns its \(q^K\) anonymous mixture labels with \(K\) categorical coordinates and a latent MEC. Chen et al. (2025) restore tensor rank through completeness and two larger-support or continuous sufficient measurements, conditions that do not cover equal-\(q\) tables.
project_justification.niche: A novel categorical double-triangular graph condition exposes square local conditional tables; an explicit diagonal-dominant family shows their joint nonvanishing locus is open and dense inside the positive categorical-table space without completeness, pure children, or larger observed alphabets.
project_justification.fill: The project delivers a field-tier exact determinant frontier, an intrinsic latent-dimension theorem, an explicit coordinate-alignment theorem that upgrades anonymous \(q^K\) mixture labels to \(K\) categorical coordinates and a latent MEC, fixed-dimension quotient identification over an enumerated alternative domain, a dense positive ternary witness with displayed matrices, and a concrete recovery handle for CDM diagnostics.

body.related_work: Lee and Gu (2026, Theorems 1--2, Appendix D, and Appendix G) supply the binary proof template and isolate the categorical determinant obstruction. Their binary assumptions and conclusions are recorded in a separately typed \(q_{\mathrm{bin}}=2\) comparator; the categorical graph condition and local-minor certificate are distinct theorem objects restricted to \(q\ge3\). Chen et al. (2025, Proposition 4.2, Definition D.3, Theorem 4.19, and Remark D.11) identify mixed-type latent structures using completeness and two sufficient measurements; their discrete sufficient measurements have support strictly larger than the latent support, so their result does not contain the equal-\(q\) certified class, while their continuous and non-triangular models prevent reverse containment. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) provide three-view Kruskal uniqueness once two full-rank views are established, but that theorem returns one \(q^K\)-class variable only up to arbitrary label permutation; the component-equality theorem supplies the additional alignment into \(K\) \(q\)-state coordinates, measurement adjacency, and a latent MEC. Gu (2026) organizes constructive unfolding queries under two pure items per attribute. Kivva et al. (2021) separate graph, state-alignment, latent-law, and latent-DAG recovery while assuming a mixture oracle; their modular decomposition informs the coordinate-alignment target but does not furnish it from \(P_X\). Gu (2025) motivates explicit polynomial exceptional sets. Gu and Xu (2021) provide binary \(Q\)-matrix criteria used by current software, and Gu et al. (2018) provide the adjacent calibrated-testing template.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The population algorithm receives exact probabilities and may query exact ranks and determinants. Finite-sample soundness cannot follow by arbitrary thresholding; the empirical question therefore fixes a separation margin and a singular-intersection branch.
body.honest_scope: For \(q\ge3\), the determinant factorization, exact frontier, open-dense nonvanishing theorem, Chen-class noncoverage relation, intrinsic dimension, observable coordinate alignment, fixed-\(K\) quotient identification, and ternary witness are theorem targets. The separately declared \(q_{\mathrm{bin}}=2\) comparator records the published Lee--Gu binary full-rank, dimension, and identification conclusions on their own binary domains. A terminating sound-and-complete local-query algorithm and simultaneous sampling calibration remain open. Unequal latent cardinalities, observed alphabets smaller than \(q\), observed-to-observed edges, and identification beyond the latent MEC are outside scope.
